name: Potiphar
overview: Potiphar is a male figure identified as an officer of Pharaoh, as noted in Genesis 37:36. Scripture does not provide information about his tribe or additional personal details. His role as a high-ranking Egyptian official situates him within the context of Egypt's governance under Pharaoh.
namesAndTitles: The name Potiphar means 'he whom Ra gives,' reflecting an Egyptian origin connected to the sun god Ra. This proper name is not indicated as given by God, highlighting its cultural background as recorded in Genesis 37:36.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Potiphar beyond his position as Pharaoh's officer. There are no listed relatives or connections beyond his official capacity.
scriptureSignificance: Potiphar's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as a prominent Egyptian official during the time of Joseph. His position under Pharaoh situates him as a key figure in the unfolding story of Joseph's life and the providential preservation of God's people. Though details are limited, Potiphar's status establishes the setting for important developments in God's plan as revealed in Genesis.
